item.title: Warren County girl, 14, in custody after allegedly shooting 8-year-old - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
WARREN COUNTY — A 14-year-old girl is reportedly in custody after allegedly shooting an 8-year-old Monday afternoon, according to WJTV.

Warren County Sheriff Martin Pace told reporters the shooting happened just before 4 p.m. on Abraham Drive.

The 8-year-old victim was transported to a hospital in Jackson for treatment. The child’s condition has not been released.

Deputies recovered a handgun at the scene, Pace said.

Darkhorse Press has reached out to Sheriff Pace for more information on whether the 14-year-old is being charged.

Authorities have not released a possible motive in the shooting. This is a developing story.

item.title: VA medical center to host veterans food pantry in Jackson on April 18 - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – The G.V. (Sonny) Montgomery VA Medical Center will host its monthly Veterans Food Pantry on Saturday, April 18, 2026, at its main campus in Jackson.

The drive-thru event is scheduled from 9 a.m. to 11 a.m. at the front entrance of the medical center.

According to the VA medical center, the pantry will provide perishable and nonperishable food to veterans experiencing food insecurity.

The event is being led by the Center for Development and Civic Engagement, formerly known as Voluntary Service.

More information is available through the G.V. (Sonny) Montgomery VA Medical Center.

item.title: Two plead guilty in trafficking case involving "largest fentanyl seizure in Southaven history" - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
HERNANDO – Two men have been convicted in a fentanyl trafficking case involving what prosecutors say was the largest fentanyl seizure in Southaven history.

The DeSoto County District Attorney’s Office announced that Michael Walker and Richard Vaught both pleaded guilty Tuesday in DeSoto County Circuit Court to trafficking charges.

According to prosecutors, the case involved 4,387 lethal dosage units of fentanyl recovered during a late 2022 operation by the Southaven Police Department at the Homewood Suites off Airways Boulevard in Southaven.

Authorities said the fentanyl had been pressed to look like oxycodone pills and carried “M 30” imprints, making the pills appear nearly identical to legitimate prescription medication.

Richard Vaught was sentenced to 15 years day for day in the custody of the Mississippi Department of Corrections, followed by 10 years of post-release supervision. Prosecutors said Walker pleaded guilty as well and will be sentenced at a later date.

Assistant District Attorney Gordon Shaw, who prosecuted the case, said fentanyl poses an extreme danger to the public.

“Fentanyl has been designated as a weapon of mass destruction for a reason,” Shaw said. “Taking this amount of narcotics off the street has undoubtedly saved lives and helped dismantle a dangerous network of drug trafficking.”

item.title: Two face charges following vandalism at Pearl City Park - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
PEARL — Two 18-year-olds are facing charges in connection with vandalism at Pearl City Park that caused an estimated $2,000 in damage, authorities said.

Officers with the Pearl Police Department first encountered the suspects, identified as John Dearing and Ashton Maples, around 2:30 a.m. March 15 while on patrol in the park after hours. Police said both individuals were in possession of spray paint cans at the time, but were released pending further investigation after no damage was immediately located.

On March 18, the city’s Parks and Recreation Division reported multiple instances of vandalism throughout the park.

Damaged property included a tennis and pickleball court, a fenced gate near a dumpster, a “No Trespassing” sign and a building at the Center City Baseball Complex, according to police.

Investigators later identified Dearing as a suspect and took him into custody. He is being held on bond pending charges of malicious mischief and trespassing.

Maples remains at large and has active warrants with the city, authorities said.

Anyone with information on Maples’ whereabouts is urged to contact the Pearl Police Department at 601-939-7000 or submit a tip through Mississippi Crime Stoppers at 1-888-8CRIMES.

All suspects are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

item.title: Teen Killed in Hattiesburg Shooting; Suspect Sought - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
HATTIESBURG — A 17-year-old boy died after being shot Sunday evening at a residence in Hattiesburg, authorities said.

Officers with the Hattiesburg Police Department responded around 7:56 p.m. April 12 to a reported shooting in the 900 block of Cypress Avenue. Upon arrival, they found the teen suffering from a gunshot wound to the chest.

The victim was transported to a local hospital, where he later died. The case is being investigated as a homicide.

Witnesses told investigators the suspect fled the scene in a dark-colored SUV immediately after the shooting. Preliminary findings indicate the suspect and victim are related, police said.

Detectives are actively working to identify the suspect and locate the vehicle involved.

Anyone with information, including surveillance footage or details about the vehicle, is urged to contact the Hattiesburg Police Department or Metro Crime Stoppers by dialing **TIPS.

Authorities said additional information will be released as it becomes available.

item.title: Stressed out? Stop and look up on National Look Up at the Sky Day - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MISSISSIPPI — National Look Up at the Sky Day, observed annually on April 14, encourages people to take a break from their daily routines and appreciate the sky and its ever-changing beauty, according to NationalToday.com.

With Artemis 2 NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen now safely back on land after they splashed down four days ago, there are still so many things to anticipate, look up at, and breathe… which is really good for your mental health, as it turns out.

The meaning of today is to invite people to look up and reflect on the vast expanse above them, serving as a reminder to be more mindful of nature, and hopefully less stressed about the noise and constancy of the every day rat race.

The origins of the day are unclear, but several sources cited by NationalToday.com suggest it may have been inspired by Jack Borden, a former Boston news reporter. Borden allegedly had a life-changing moment in 1978 when he stopped from his busy life and looked up at the sky “for the first time,” later founding the nonprofit For Spacious Skies to encourage others to appreciate the natural world.

The organization focused on teaching both children and adults to be present and aware of their surroundings. NationalToday.com also cites a Harvard study indicating that students who were more aware of the sky performed better in subjects such as reading, writing, music and visual arts.

Throughout history, the sky has played a significant role in science, religion and navigation. According to NationalToday.com, ancient civilizations such as the Mayans studied celestial objects closely, often linking them to gods and using them to create calendars. Early sailors relied on the stars for navigation, while the sun served as a primary way to track time.

Astronomy is considered the oldest natural science, and interest in the sky continues today through organizations like NASA, which has studied space since its founding in 1958.

Modern-day skywatchers also have opportunities to observe celestial events. According to AccuWeather, April’s Lyrid meteor shower, which is one of the oldest known with records dating back about 2,700 years, is expected to peak April 21 into April 22, producing up to 15 to 20 meteors per hour under favorable conditions.

Additional sky events this month include a planetary alignment featuring Mercury, Mars, Jupiter and Neptune, visible in the early morning hours later in April, according to CNET.

National Look Up at the Sky Day serves as a reminder that the sky holds both historical significance and present-day wonder for those who take the time to notice it. Plus, it’s good for your heart (in a lot of ways).

item.title: Rankin County Animal Shelter to host adoption event in Brandon - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
BRANDON – The Rankin County Animal Shelter will hold an adoption event Saturday at Petsense by Tractor Supply in Brandon.

The event is scheduled from 9:30 a.m. until noon at 315 Crossgates Blvd.

Shelter officials said the public is invited to stop by and meet adoptable animals. They also encouraged supporters who may not be looking to adopt to visit the event and shop for toys or treats for their pets.

The shelter said it hopes to see community members there Saturday.

item.title: Mississippi Enacts Sweeping Law Targeting Gang Violence - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Mississippi has enacted a sweeping new law aimed at reducing gang-related violence and crimes involving minors and firearms, state officials announced.

Attorney General Lynn Fitch said Senate Bill 2710, signed into law as part of her 2026 legislative agenda, targets gang activity by increasing penalties and shifting how certain juvenile firearm cases are prosecuted.

The law moves crimes of violence involving a firearm out of youth court and into circuit court, increases penalties for transferring stolen firearms to minors, and enhances sentences when stolen guns are used in violent crimes — including up to 40 years if used in a murder.

It also creates a new criminal offense for shooting into a crowd, with stricter penalties if the incident occurs at places such as schools, churches, courthouses, playgrounds or parks, or if minors are present or the offender is a gang member.

“There are more than 200 gangs in Mississippi, and they recruit minors to do a lot of their dirty work, knowing that punishment is often disproportionate to the severity of the crime,” Fitch said. “Now the penalty fits the crime, making juvenile recruitment less attractive and getting dangerous criminals off the street.”

Fitch said the measure also responds to recent incidents of violence at public gatherings, including high school and college football games and homecoming events that left nearly a dozen people dead and dozens injured last fall.

The bill received support from several law enforcement and municipal organizations, including the Mississippi Prosecutors Association, the Mississippi Association of Chiefs of Police, the Mississippi Municipal League and the Mississippi Sheriffs’ Association.

Bryan Buckley, president of the Mississippi Prosecutors Association and an assistant district attorney, said the law will help curb gun violence by minors and those who provide them with firearms.

Police Chief Billy Seal, president of the Mississippi Association of Chiefs of Police, called the legislation “a critical step forward” in addressing gang-related violence and protecting communities, particularly young people.

Shari Veazey, executive director of the Mississippi Municipal League, said cities and towns have seen a rise in youth and gang-related crime and that the law will provide needed support to improve public safety.

The bill was introduced by Sen. Joey Fillingane and is one of several measures from Fitch’s legislative agenda to become law this year. Lawmakers also approved two bills aimed at strengthening the state’s response to human trafficking and another to enhance child support enforcement.

item.title: Maryland Kidnapping Suspects Arrested in Columbia; Infant Found Safe - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
COLUMBIA — Two people wanted on kidnapping charges out of Maryland have been arrested in Marion County, and an infant reported missing has been found safe, authorities said.

Celso Galvez Morales was taken into custody April 11 after officers with the Columbia Police Department conducted a traffic stop for speeding during proactive patrol.

During the stop, officers discovered Morales was a fugitive wanted in Maryland on kidnapping charges. A 4-month-old child in the vehicle was safely recovered and turned over to the Mississippi Department of Child Protective Services.

As the investigation continued, officers determined Morales’ girlfriend, Laura Ignacio Martinez, was also wanted in Maryland on kidnapping charges.

Police located and arrested Martinez the following day, April 12, without incident.

Both suspects are being held pending extradition to Maryland.

Authorities confirmed the juvenile connected to the case has been found safe following coordination with the Forrest County Sheriff’s Office.

Columbia Police Chief Fortenberry praised the officers involved, citing the importance of proactive policing and attention to detail.

All individuals are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

item.title: Man Shot at Monroe County Field Party; Deputies Make Arrests for Interference - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MONROE COUNTY — A 44-year-old man was shot Saturday night during a large gathering in Monroe County, according to the sheriff’s office.

Monroe County 911 dispatch received a call around 10 p.m. reporting weapons being pulled and shots fired at a field party on Jakobi Lane near Shepherd Drive and Highway 45 Alternate. While deputies were en route, a caller reported that someone had been shot.

When deputies arrived, they were initially unable to enter the area due to heavy traffic leaving the scene. Once they gained access, they found the victim alive with a gunshot wound to the upper torso.

Authorities said deputies had to arrest multiple individuals at the scene for interfering with their efforts to render aid to the victim.

Emergency responders with Medstat transported the victim to North Mississippi Medical Center in Tupelo. His condition has not been released.

Investigators said no one at the scene was willing to provide information about who fired the shots or what led to the violence.

Sheriff Kevin Crook is asking anyone with information to contact the Monroe County Sheriff’s Office at 662-369-2468. Tipsters can also remain anonymous by contacting Golden Triangle Crime Stoppers at 1-800-530-7151.

item.title: Man Arrested in Dundee Trail Ride Shooting Investigation - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
DUNDEE — A man has been arrested in connection with a shooting that occurred during a trail ride event in Dundee last month, authorities said.

Malik Javonta Vardaman, 27, of Robinsonville, was taken into custody April 11 by the Tunica County Sheriff’s Office.

The arrest stems from a March 28 shooting at a trail ride hosted on Dubbs Road by Muddy River Delta Farm.

Investigators said warrants were issued April 6 by a circuit court judge charging Vardaman with aggravated assault and discharging a firearm.

Authorities have not released additional details about the circumstances of the shooting or any victims.

The investigation remains ongoing. Anyone with information is urged to contact the Tunica County Sheriff’s Office at 662-363-1411 or Crime Stoppers at 662-910-0400. Officials said tips leading to an arrest could be eligible for a reward of up to $1,000.

item.title: Man arrested following search warrant in Lauderdale County narcotics investigation - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Greer Vari
item.description:
LAUDERDALE COUNTY – One person is in custody following a search warrant executed Tuesday morning in connection with an ongoing narcotics and stolen property investigation, according to the Lauderdale County Sheriff’s Department.

Deputies with the department’s Narcotics and SWAT units carried out the search at approximately 6:30 a.m. in the 5900 block of Cuba Road, where authorities recovered narcotics and items believed to be stolen.

Primus Williams, 54, was arrested and charged with multiple offenses, including sale of methamphetamine while in possession of a firearm, possession of methamphetamine with intent to distribute while in possession of a firearm, possession of oxycodone with intent to distribute while in possession of a firearm, and possession of a stolen firearm.

Authorities said the search warrant followed a lengthy investigation that remains ongoing, with additional charges possible.

Williams’ bond was set at $100,000 for each controlled substance charge, $100,000 for possession of a stolen firearm and $100,000 for the enhanced penalty related to drug possession while armed, for a total of $400,000.

He is being held at the Lauderdale County Detention Facility.

item.title: JPD asks for public help identifying woman in video - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Police are asking the public’s help to identify a woman seen on camera break out panes in a window in what appears to be a home.

In the video, it appears that the woman uses a piece of a brick to break out at least four panes of a window in a home.

The Jackson Police Department asks that if you know her identity and whereabouts, you would please contact them at 601-960-1800 or Crime Stoppers at 601-355-TIPS.

item.title: Jackson man shot while sleeping in his bed - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – A Jackson man was asleep when he was shot on Summit Street last night.

According to Detective Tommie Brown, with the Jackson Police Department, the man was sleeping and was woken up when he heard multiple gunshots.

The victim noticed he had been shot several times.

Detective Brown said he didn’t know who the shooters are or why are were shooting into his home.

He has been listed in stable condition.

item.title: Jackson County woman charged with child abuse - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON COUNTY – A Jackson County woman has been charged with child abuse following an investigation that began in September 2025, according to the Jackson County Sheriff’s Office.

Sheriff John Ledbetter said Melissa Pearson, 46, was charged April 9, 2026. The charge stems from an incident involving a juvenile known to Pearson, according to the sheriff’s office.

Authorities said Pearson’s bond was set at $25,000. The Mississippi Department of Corrections also charged her with a probation violation.

Because the case involves a juvenile, no further details were released.

item.title: Hattiesburg police seek help identifying armed robbery suspect on Lincoln Road - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
HATTIESBURG – The Hattiesburg Police Department is asking for the public’s help in identifying a suspect after an armed robbery Tuesday afternoon on Lincoln Road.

Police said the robbery happened around 4:05 p.m. April 7 in the 1800 block of Lincoln Road.

According to investigators, a man entered a business and demanded money. The suspect was described as wearing a gray sweatshirt, black pants, black-and-white shoes and a gray hat.

item.title: George County investigation leads to child exploitation arrest in New York - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
GEORGE COUNTY – A George County investigation into a possible child exploitation case has led to the arrest of a New York man now facing a federal charge, according to the George County Sheriff’s Office.

Authorities said a George County resident reported the case to the sheriff’s office Criminal Investigation Division on Dec. 15, 2025.

During the investigation, officials learned the child and the suspect first made contact through a popular online gaming platform before later exchanging phone numbers, according to the sheriff’s office. Investigators said the relationship escalated to the point that the child was sending personal images to the suspect.

Through a joint effort involving George County investigators, detectives in Glens Falls, New York, and Homeland Security Investigations, authorities secured a search warrant for the suspect’s home and electronic devices.

On March 9, 2026, 30-year-old Dylan Taylor of Glens Falls was arrested, according to the sheriff’s office. Officials said Taylor has been charged with one count of receiving child pornography and is being held in federal custody.

The investigation remains ongoing.

Sheriff Mitchell Mixon said the case shows the value of cooperation between agencies.

“This case highlights the positive results that come from strong collaboration between agencies at all levels,” Mixon said. “We will continue to utilize every available resource to protect our children and hold offenders accountable.”

item.title: Delta Correctional Facility graduates 16 in substance disorder programs - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
GREENWOOD — VitalCore Health Strategies’ Long-Term Substance Use Disorder Program at Delta Correctional Facility has graduated 16 participants.

The participants completed courses such as Celebrate Recovery, Moral Reconation Therapy, Anger Management, Living in Balance, A New Direction, and the 12 Step Program during the six-month program. Evangelist Pamela Hilton gave them an encouraging message at the graduation. Her focal point was “I Can” versus “I Can’t”.

Singing and praise dances were a part of the graduation. The graduates performed a skit reflecting on what they have learned and experienced in life. Also, they not only recited the 12 steps but learned to work them.

The program was hosted by the SUD Counselor, Whitney Cosey. The theme was Paris, the City of Light. Cosey said she has seen each graduate’s light grow through their effort and commitment during the program.

The graduates are to continue to remain sober, work the 12 steps daily, and take accountability for their actions.

item.title: DARKHORSE DOGS: Puttie Belle, the perfect child-loving dog needs a loving home - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
BROOKHAVEN – A young dog at the Brookhaven Animal Rescue League has been waiting nearly a year for a home, and shelter volunteers say time in the shelter is beginning to take a toll.

Puttie Belle, a perfect 1 1/2-year-old dog weighing 44 pounds, has been at BARL for 11 months and is still looking for a family.

According to the shelter, Puttie Belle gets time in the play yard every day, but staff say what she really needs is a permanent home.

Shelter supporters describe her as energetic, happy and friendly. They say she has done well with a special needs child in a previous home and is also good with other children.

Puttie Belle is known for standing up to greet people, but supporters say she is polite and does not put her feet on them.

According to BARL, she is fine around cows and plays well with some dogs, though she can be selective with others. She is not considered a good fit for homes with chickens, and shelter staff believe she is probably not suited for homes with cats.

Puttie Belle is the sweetest girl and she so needs to get out of the shelter and into a loving home! Go visit her this week and see if she is a good fit for your family!

Those interested in meeting Puttie Belle can visit BARL from noon to 3 p.m. Thursday through Sunday or call or text 601-757-3211 to schedule an appointment at other times.

item.title: 4 arrested after Jones County drug raid at Ellisville home - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JONES COUNTY – Jones County Sheriff’s Department narcotics agents and criminal investigators executed a search warrant Monday at a house on East Oak Street in Ellisville, where authorities said they found methamphetamine, cocaine, ecstasy and firearms.

According to the sheriff’s department, the search warrant stemmed from complaints from nearby residents and a lengthy investigation.

Investigators said agents found about 6.4 ounces, or 181 grams, of methamphetamine, 14 grams of powder cocaine and 22 dosage units of ecstasy. Deputies also recovered two firearms, one of which had been reported stolen out of Laurel.

Four people were arrested at the residence.

Authorities identified those arrested as Brandon Barnes, who is charged with trafficking a controlled substance, methamphetamine, and possession of a controlled substance, cocaine and ecstasy; Elizabeth Garcia, who is charged with trafficking of methamphetamine and possession of a stolen firearm; Desmond Evans, who is charged with possession of methamphetamine while in possession of a firearm; and Bridgette Jefcoat, who was arrested on a Mississippi Department of Corrections warrant.

“Sheriff Joe Berlin has made it clear that if you are on his radar dealing and/or possessing illegal narcotics that you should sleep with one eye open because we are coming for you,” JCSD Narcotics Division Sgt. Chase Smith said.

Smith added, “We have plenty of leads to follow up on and we are constantly working investigations and building solid cases. The best advice I can give you is to find a new, legal career to pursue and not illegal narcotics possession and distribution.”

item.title: State auditor demands private prison company repay $7.4 million to Mississippi taxpayers - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Mississippi State Auditor Shad White announced Thursday that his office is demanding more than $7.4 million from private prison company Management & Training Corporation, saying the company failed to provide the staffing required under its contracts with the state.

According to the Mississippi Office of the State Auditor, the civil demands have also been referred to the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office for enforcement in court.

White said the auditor’s office began investigating MTC after allegations surfaced that the company was not providing the prison staff required by its contracts with the state. Investigators found that MTC failed to provide the minimum mandatory staffing levels intended to help ensure the safety of inmates and prison employees, but billed the state as though those requirements had been met, the auditor’s office said.

The auditor’s office issued three separate demands: $462,299.32 tied to staffing credits invoiced to the Mississippi Department of Corrections for the East Mississippi Correctional Facility, $959,240.06 for the Marshall County Correctional Facility and $6,002,027.92 for the Wilkinson County Correctional Facility.

“This is one of the largest civil demands made in the history of the Auditor’s Office,” White said. “We’re now turning this case over to the AG’s Office for enforcement to ensure accountability for taxpayers, and I hope they will litigate the case immediately.”

White also said his office will pursue repayment regardless of the size or influence of the company involved.

“I don’t care how big of an out-of-state company you are or how many campaign donations you make to the other politicians, if you owe taxpayers money because you failed to live up to a contract with government, we will demand you pay it back,” White said. “No free rides on the backs of taxpayers.”

The case has been referred to the attorney general’s office for possible court action.

item.title: Hinds County Courthouse, Clerk’s Office Evacuated After Threat of Possible Hazardous Device - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The Hinds County Circuit Courthouse and the Hinds County Circuit Clerk’s Office were evacuated Monday following a reported threat involving a potential hazardous device, authorities said.

The Hinds County Sheriff’s Office said the evacuation will remain in effect until further notice as deputies and assisting law enforcement agencies respond to the scene.

Officials have not released details about the nature of the threat or whether a device has been located.

Additional law enforcement partners are assisting in the response as the situation remains under investigation.

No injuries have been reported. Authorities have not said when the buildings may reopen.

item.title: ‘Fondren Firebug’ sentenced on trespassing charge in CCID Court - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch announced the recent sentencing of Todd Bryan Higgins, 52, known as the “Fondren Firebug,” on a trespassing conviction in Capitol Complex Improvement District Court.

According to the attorney general’s office, Higgins was sentenced April 8, 2026, by CCID Court Judge James Holland to six months in the custody of the Hinds County Detention Center, with five months to serve followed by one month of probation.

The case was investigated by Capitol Police and prosecuted by the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office.

The court also took note of Higgins’ prior interactions with law enforcement dating back to 2020, including indictments for third-degree arson and grand larceny, according to the attorney general’s office.

In announcing the sentence, Fitch also highlighted the work of the CCID Court since its creation. The attorney general’s office said it secured nearly 300 convictions in CCID Court in 2025 with a 98% success rate.

So far in 2026, prosecutors with the office have handled more than 300 initial appearances, more than 50 preliminary hearings, nearly 70 misdemeanor trials and nearly 550 traffic violations before the court, according to the attorney general’s office.

“Our office was proud to defend the law creating the CCID Court against both state and federal challenges,” Fitch said. “We were proud to work with the judges, law enforcement, prosecutors, and public defenders to stand up the court just over a year ago. And we are proud to work each day to prosecute the offenses that come before the CCID judges. We are committed to ensuring that our capital city is safe.”

item.title: Arkansas man extradited to Tupelo in attempted ATM break-in case - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUPELO – A man from Arkansas has been extradited to Tupelo and charged in connection with an attempted break-in at a bank ATM, according to the Tupelo Police Department.

Police said Farmers & Merchants Bank at 1803 W. Main St. reported an attempted break-in of its ATM on March 16, 2026.

During the investigation, Tupelo detectives worked with multiple law enforcement agencies, including police departments in Pelham, Alabama; Dallas; Booneville; Pontotoc; and Bentonville, Arkansas, as well as the Mississippi Bureau of Investigation and the St. Francis County, Arkansas, Sheriff’s Department, authorities said.

After further investigation, 30-year-old Edwin Abraham Cardenas Figuera of Bentonville, Arkansas, was arrested April 6 by Bentonville police and extradited to Tupelo, according to police.

Authorities said Cardenas Figuera was charged with attempted grand larceny.

At an initial appearance April 10 in Tupelo Municipal Court, Judge Jay Weir denied bond, police said.

item.title: 2 arrested after Claiborne County drive-by shooting in Sugar Hill area - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
CLAIBORNE COUNTY – Two people were arrested after a reported drive-by shooting late at night on Elmwood Street in the Sugar Hill area, according to the Claiborne County Sheriff’s Office.

Authorities said deputies responded around 11:19 p.m. to a report of shots fired. A caller reported hearing multiple gunshots and seeing a black vehicle with chrome wheels leaving the area at a high rate of speed.

Deputies and the sheriff responded immediately and, while canvassing the area, spotted a black vehicle matching the description traveling from Highway 547. A traffic stop was initiated, and the occupants were detained without incident, the sheriff’s office said.

During the stop, the driver told deputies a firearm was on the back seat of the vehicle and gave consent to search it, according to investigators. Deputies said they recovered a firearm and other evidence from the vehicle.

Further investigation found the shell casings and bullets recovered from the vehicle were consistent with evidence found at the original scene, authorities said. Deputies also collected four .223 shell casings from the scene.

Investigators said both suspects admitted involvement in the shooting, which stemmed from an ongoing dispute with a person living at 1013 Elmwood St.

The sheriff’s office identified those arrested as Javeion Perkins, born April 18, 2006, of Vicksburg, and Arkeem Banks, born Nov. 4, 2007, also of Vicksburg.

Both made initial appearances before Judge Flowers, who set bond at $50,000 each.

Sheriff Edward L. Goods Sr. thanked the deputies for their quick response and arrest of the suspects.
